The passage describes the Treaty of Tordesillas, which divided newly discovered lands between Spain and Portugal along a meridian 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde Islands. Portugal received territories east of the line, while Spain received those to the west.  

By 1494, Portuguese explorers had already begun establishing a sea route to India by sailing around Africa—Bartolomeu Dias had rounded the Cape of Good Hope in 1488, and Vasco da Gama would reach India in 1498. Securing the eastern route ensured Portugal’s access to the lucrative spice trade and territories in Africa and Asia, without conflicting with Spanish claims in the Americas.  

Option (D) fits this context: the Portuguese knew of a route to India via the Cape of Good Hope and wanted to protect their trade interests east of the demarcation line.  

Final answer: (D)
